newsitem.title: USA: Former Texaco treasurer pleads not guilty.
newsitem.headline: Former Texaco treasurer pleads not guilty.

text.p: Texaco Inc.'s former treasurer pleaded innocent Thursday to charges he ordered the destruction of documents in a highly publicised racial discrimination case against the nation's third largest oil company.

Robert Ulrich, the retired corporate treasurer, was indicted by a federal grand jury in White Plains, N.Y., last week on one count each of conspiracy and obstruction of justice. He is scheduled to appear in White Plains federal court on July 10 for the next hearing in the case.

He is the second former Texaco executive to be charged in the case. Richard Lundwall, senior coordinator for personnel services in Texaco's finance department, was indicted in March on a charge of obstruction of justice.
The indictment issued Friday is an expansion of the earlier charge against Lundwall and adds one count of conspiracy against him as well.
If convicted, both men face up to 15 years in prison.
The case against the men stems from Lundwall's decision to provide evidence against himself and his colleagues in the racial discrimination case against Texaco.
In a lawsuit filed in 1994, a group of black employees alleged that Texaco discriminated against them in promotions and pay.

Lundwall had secretly taped conversations between himself and others in which they discussed destroying documents requested by the plaintiffs. When Lundwall was dismissed by Texaco in a downsizing move last summer, he gave the tapes to the plaintiffs' lawyers.
The indictment alleges Ulrich directed Lundwall to "shred" and "get rid of" certain documents.
After the tapes were made public in court proceedings, Texaco agreed last November to settle the case for a record $176.1 million, according to plaintiffs' attorneys.
